thought: his feet ache; he still thinks about the Christmas the Duke gave him a chair
line: The Duke gave me a chair once, you know. From his own room.

thought: another treasure hunter has just been sent to him with a scroll
line: Treasure hunters again. Why does every scroll send them to me?

thought: someone raised their voice in the courtyard and it brought back the stranger who threatened them all
line: Still can't hear a raised voice without thinking of that awful man.

thought: rehearsing the directions he gives every lost newcomer
line: North over the river for Varrock, upstairs for the Duke.

thought: keeping his direction on the round
line: Clockwise, always clockwise. The other way would feel all wrong.

thought: word came that someone has mastered every skill; he sends his congratulations by magic
line: Another one's mastered every skill. I'll send my congratulations.

thought: caught pausing, he has an excuse ready
line: If anyone asks, I'm not resting. I'm inspecting the flagstones.

thought: the day's fresh arrivals, eager as they always are
line: New faces in the courtyard again. They all look so keen.

thought: he remembers how long this one has been about, and it suits them
line: You've been about a good while now. It shows, in a nice way.

thought: they don't stop to ask the way; he checks himself and is pleased
line: Not lost, are you? No, you know your way now.

thought: an armed stranger passed and he didn't startle
line: You didn't make me jump at all. Most strangers make me jump.

thought: he remembers every face, and this one fondly
line: I never forget a face, and yours I'm always glad of.

thought: points them out to someone: he saw them arrive, green
line: Look at that one. Came through here green as grass, once.

thought: they walk like someone with business elsewhere now
line: Off somewhere grand, I expect. You've that walk about you now.

thought: most people want directions or a clue casket from him; this one wants nothing
line: A face that wants neither directions nor a casket. How refreshing.

thought: as the Duke's servant he'd put in a word for a polite one
line: If the Duke ever asks who's polite round here, I'll say you.

thought: assumes they're lost again and gives the same directions, pointedly
line: Lost again? Varrock's north over the river, same as last time.

thought: they came in briskly and frightened him; it reminded him of the man who threatened everyone
line: Must you stride in like that? I thought it was that man again.

thought: they're crossing his round the wrong way
line: Clockwise, if you please. You're walking against the flow.

thought: he remembers them arriving eager; the eagerness seems to have gone
line: You arrived looking so eager. Whatever happened to that?

thought: grumbles to someone nearby that this one never greets him
line: That one's never once stopped to say hello. Not once.

thought: adventurers rush through his courtyard without a wave
line: Adventurers. Always in a rush, and not one of them waves.

thought: he hands caskets to treasure hunters; this one just looks the grasping type
line: No casket for you. You just look like someone who'd want one.

thought: he's watched countless newcomers; this one is merely one of them
line: Seen ever so many come through, and you're... well, one of them.

thought: his back still hurts from the day clearing the cellar
line: All day clearing that cellar. My back's still complaining.

thought: he didn't feel any earthquake but won't doubt the Duke
line: An earthquake, the Duke says. I never felt it, but he'd know.

thought: rubble isn't a servant's job
line: Rubble, rubble, rubble... I'm a servant, not a mole.

thought: the cellar frightens him now
line: Nobody's getting me back in that cellar. Not after the wall went.

thought: he has his escape planned for the next tremor
line: If the ground shakes again, I'll be first under the table.

thought: the Cook has been grumbling about dust in the ingredients
line: Cook's still finding cellar dust in his flour. He's not pleased.

thought: the Duke is waiting on builders and Hans is watching for them
line: Still no builders for that cellar wall. I keep watching the bridge.

thought: only one wall came down; he counts it a mercy
line: Funny sort of earthquake, just the one wall. Lucky, really.

thought: this one looks steady; he'd want them about in a tremor
line: You've a steady look. I'd want you about if the ground shook again.

thought: they're heading indoors near the cellar, which he won't go near
line: Going near that cellar? You're braver than I am.

thought: he swept all day and they haven't tracked anything in
line: Thank you for not treading rubble about. I swept all day.

thought: a calm face after weeks of nerves
line: A calm face, at last. I've been all nerves since the wall fell in.

thought: this one wouldn't panic the way he does
line: That one'd not run screaming from an earthquake. Not like some.

thought: an adventurer would have cleared the rubble much faster than him
line: You'd have cleared that cellar in half the time, I expect.

thought: the Duke is waiting on builders; he'd put this one forward
line: If the Duke wants strong arms for that wall, I'll mention you.

thought: walls coming down and this one is perfectly cheerful
line: Walls falling in, and you strolling about cheerful as anything.

thought: misattribution: perhaps this clumsy adventurer knocked the wall in
line: Not you who knocked the cellar wall in, is it? You've the elbows.

thought: they have time for adventures but nobody helped him sweep
line: Plenty of time for adventures, I see. None for sweeping.

thought: their footsteps made him think the cellar was going again
line: Heavy-footed, aren't you? I thought the cellar was going again.

thought: stomping adventurers and falling walls, in his mind connected
line: Adventurers. Stomp about all day, and then walls fall in.

thought: offers them the rubble job, knowing the answer
line: Want a job? There's rubble, if you're not too grand for it.

thought: loyal to the Duke's account, suspects the stranger of spreading talk
line: Don't go saying the castle's falling down. It was an earthquake.

thought: this one would run at the next tremor, though Hans would be first
line: That one would be first out the gate if it shook again. After me.

thought: nobody brave has gone to look at the cellar
line: Brave adventurers everywhere, and not one went down for a look.

thought: he's delighted with the new neighbours
line: Goblins under the castle! I wave down the cellar steps of a morning.

thought: some in town dislike the treaty; he likes it
line: Not everyone likes the treaty, but I do. Lovely quiet neighbours.

thought: the Duke is keeping the cellar hole open for trade
line: The hole's staying, for trade, the Duke says. Very forward-thinking.

thought: the household has changed: adviser out, goblins in
line: Sigmund gone, and goblins in the cellar. Funny old castle.

thought: he was frightened of the cellar, and the goblins turned out pleasant
line: I was so jumpy about that cellar. Turns out they're ever so polite.

thought: working out who owns what under the treaty
line: Below ground's theirs, except the cellars. Those are ours, I think.

thought: goblin neighbours make less mess than adventurers
line: Quieter than adventurers, goblins. Much kinder to the floors.

thought: it surprises him that he of all people has goblin neighbours
line: Fancy me with goblin neighbours. Who'd have thought it?

thought: this is the one who made peace below; his nerves are better for it
line: You sorted things with the goblins, didn't you? I sleep better now.

thought: tells someone this is the one who brought back a treaty
line: That's the one who went down the cellar and came back with a treaty.

thought: he remembers them new and lost, and now there's peace
line: You arrived not knowing the way, and now there's a treaty.

thought: he would never have gone down the hole
line: I'd never have gone down that hole. You did, and look what came of it.

thought: someone wanted a war with the goblins; this one found peace
line: Some wanted a war with the goblins. You found a better way.

thought: the castle is calmer and so is he
line: The castle's quieter for what you did. My nerves thank you.

thought: recognises them crossing the courtyard
line: Oh, it's you! The one who made friends under the castle.

thought: he heard Sigmund hid the silverware and guesses this one found out
line: Sigmund hid the silverware, they say. You found him out, I'll bet.

thought: they went straight down the hole; he'd have fainted
line: Straight down a goblin hole, you went. I'd have fainted, and sensibly.

thought: peace is made but they still march about like a soldier
line: All that peace, and you still march through here like it's a war.

thought: not everyone liked the treaty, and some blame them
line: Not everyone's glad of the treaty, you know. Some say it's your fault.

thought: this peacemaker still asks him the way
line: Made peace with goblins, and still asks me the way to Varrock.

thought: with Sigmund dismissed, his errands fell to Hans
line: Got Sigmund thrown out, didn't you? Now I do his fetching.

thought: he'd thank them but they never stop moving, which is rich from him
line: I'd thank you properly, but you never stand still long enough.

thought: worries the goblins will pick up adventurer habits
line: Friend to goblins now, are you? Mind they don't pick up your manners.

thought: nobody asked him about the new neighbours, though he likes them
line: That one brought us goblin neighbours, and never asked how I felt.

thought: he sends everyone on errands because he can never leave
line: Errands, errands, and never once can I run one myself.

thought: remembers the lookouts his father posted against Elvarg
line: Father kept lookouts on the roof for Elvarg. I miss the company.

thought: Crandor was grand in his father's day, then went silent
line: Crandor was as grand as Falador once, you know. Then not a word.

thought: signing trading permits; prosperity means paperwork
line: Another permit to sign. Prosperity is a great deal of paperwork.

thought: watches Hans going round and approves
line: Hans has been splendidly busy today. Saradomin bless the man.

thought: he keeps a careful eye on his limited shields
line: I count my shields every evening. Adventurers come through, after all.

thought: the Cook boasts of the new range; the Duke has yet to see results
line: Cook says the new range burns less. I've yet to taste the evidence.

thought: someone asked about staff holidays; out of the question
line: Holidays for core staff? Gracious, no, who would mind the castle?

thought: this one looks useful to a duke
line: You have the look of someone who gets things done, adventurer.

thought: brave without being reckless, the quality he values
line: Brave, I'd say, but not foolish. Rarer than you'd think, that.

thought: the sort of character Lumbridge wants
line: Good day to you. Lumbridge could use more of your character.

thought: tells his servant this one has manners
line: Hans, that one has manners. Do make a note.

thought: his father would have made this one a lookout
line: My father would have had someone like you up on the roof, watching.

thought: he gives shields only for worthy causes; this one might qualify
line: Should a truly worthy cause arise... I'd think of you for a shield.

thought: notices a traveller with purpose
line: By Saradomin, a traveller with purpose! One sees so few.

thought: rank-minded: the peasantry could learn from this one
line: The peasantry could learn a great deal from your bearing.

thought: adventurers are known to help themselves
line: Do come in, by all means. The furniture is nailed down, I trust.

thought: every adventurer wants a shield
line: Another adventurer. You'll be wanting a shield too, I suppose.

thought: courage noted; restraint lacking
line: Courage is admirable. So, in its way, is a little restraint.

thought: tells Hans to watch this one near the silver
line: Hans, do keep an eye on that one near the silver.

thought: he's heard adventurers are useful; still waiting
line: One hears adventurers are terribly useful. One lives in hope.

thought: he stands only for the worthy
line: You'll forgive me if I don't stand. One stands for the worthy.

thought: he'd send them on an errand but values the errand
line: I would send you on an errand, but I'm rather fond of the errand.

thought: they came in without knocking
line: Do adventurers ever knock, or is that a knightly habit?

thought: turning the cellar talisman over in his hands
line: The household found this in the cellar... I can't stop looking at it.

thought: Sedridor should have it, but he can't leave
line: Sedridor would want this, surely. If only I could leave the castle.

thought: heard the wizards are hunting artefacts
line: The wizards hunt artefacts, I'm told. I may have just the thing.

thought: the tower isn't far, for anyone free to go
line: The Wizards' Tower is hardly far. For someone else, that is.

thought: he doesn't know what to do with it, so he polished it
line: What does one do with a talisman? I've polished it, for a start.

thought: if this was in the cellar junk, what else is?
line: Found among the junk in my own cellar. Whatever else is down there?

thought: it wants a proper adventurer, not any passing peasant
line: I shan't trust it to the peasantry. It wants someone proper.

thought: judging its age, or its dirt
line: Ancient, this talisman, or else very dirty.

thought: trustworthiness matters with a precious object
line: You look the trustworthy sort. One needs that, with a talisman.

thought: envies their freedom to travel
line: Free to come and go, aren't you? One could do great things with that.

thought: trust measured in distance to the tower
line: I'd trust you as far as the Wizards' Tower, and that's a fair way.

thought: points this one out to Hans as a possible expert
line: Hans, there goes someone who might know about talismans.

thought: they have a learned air; perhaps they know talismans
line: You've a scholarly air. Do you know anything of talismans?

thought: sensible and on foot, the kind the wizards would want
line: Sensible and on foot. Just what the wizards would want, I'd think.

thought: they could carry something curious safely
line: If anyone could carry a curious thing safely, it's you, I fancy.

thought: a capable face in his castle at last
line: Good heavens, a capable face. The castle has been short of those.

thought: doubts they'd get it past the bridge
line: You'd lose a talisman before the bridge, I expect.

thought: nobody asks about his talisman
line: Adventurers come and go, and not one of them asks about talismans.

thought: wonders if the wizards would even admit them
line: Hmm. Would the wizards even let you in, I wonder?

thought: keep this one out of the cellar; enough has turned up there
line: Hans, keep that one out of the cellar. We've found quite enough.

thought: fears they'd sell it
line: I'd ask your help, but I fear you'd sell the thing in Varrock.

thought: who let them in? anyone gets in
line: Who let you in? Oh, never mind, everyone gets in.

thought: two curiosities in the room, only one interesting
line: A curious talisman and a curious caller. Only one interests me.

thought: Sedridor wants clever people; implies this one isn't
line: Sedridor wants clever people. Do you know any?

thought: marvels that a cellar trinket led to a hidden mine
line: A hidden mine, from one little talisman in my cellar. Remarkable.

thought: he always knew it mattered, he tells himself
line: I always said that talisman mattered. I did say, didn't I?

thought: the shelf where the talisman sat is empty now
line: The wizards have their mine, and I've an empty shelf where it sat.

thought: wonders about recognition
line: I wonder if the wizards would name a seam after me. Probably not.

thought: repeats what the wizards call it, without quite understanding
line: Rune essence, the wizards call it. Terribly important, I'm told.

thought: providence working through his cellar
line: Saradomin moves in curious ways. Through my cellar, apparently.

thought: tempted to search the cellar again
line: I've half a mind to search the cellar again. The other half is wiser.

thought: the wizards got a mine and he got nothing
line: Not so much as a rune for my trouble. The wizards got a mine.

thought: recognises the one who carried his talisman
line: Ah, the one who took my talisman across! A whole mine, they tell me.

thought: they did Lumbridge credit
line: You did Lumbridge proud at the Wizards' Tower, adventurer.

thought: tells Hans to bow to the finder of the mine
line: Hans, that's the one who found the wizards their mine. Bow, man.

thought: he picked well, and says so
line: I chose well with you. One so rarely gets to say that.

thought: would trust them with all his letters now
line: Trustworthy and quick. I should have you carry all my letters.

thought: the next cellar mystery is theirs
line: Should the cellar give up another mystery, I'll send for you first.

thought: Saradomin favoured the errand and the runner
line: Saradomin smiled on that errand, and on you, I'd say.

thought: his talisman, their feet: a partnership
line: A mine found through my talisman and your feet. A fine partnership.

thought: one walk and they think themselves important
line: One walk to the Wizards' Tower, and now you're terribly important.

thought: reminds them he found the talisman; they only walked
line: I found the talisman, you'll recall. You merely walked.

thought: misattribution of who gets credit
line: Do stop telling people it was your mine. It was my cellar.

thought: warns Hans to hide anything else from the cellar
line: Hans, the talisman carrier's back. Hide anything else in the cellar.

thought: a single delivery doesn't make a wizard
line: One delivery, and you think yourself a wizard. Hmm?

thought: they're back as if expecting more treasure; he has only cutlery
line: Back again? I've no more talismans, I'm afraid, only spoons.

thought: credit is due, mostly to him
line: Credit where it's due, adventurer. Rather more of it is mine.

thought: adventurers get the glory, dukes get letters
line: Adventurers get the songs. Dukes who find talismans get a letter.

thought: the salesman's promises versus the smell of smoke
line: Temperature control and magic, the salesman said. Smells of smoke.

thought: he checked whether he could have a holiday
line: No holidays for core staff, and I'm core staff. I checked.

thought: the goat needs feeding and the children won't
line: Somebody's got to feed the goat, and it's never the children.

thought: every cake he's made has burned
line: Every cake I've ever made has burned! Every single one.

thought: the flour is fine; he's the problem
line: Millie's flour is lovely. It's what I do to it that's the trouble.

thought: touches his hat; insists he's a real cook
line: Standard cook's issue, this hat. I'm a real cook, whatever they say.

thought: wonders what the Duke's table is like with unburnt food
line: Wonder what the Duke's table looks like with food that isn't burnt.

thought: Hans keeps passing the kitchen window; he feels judged
line: Hans keeps passing the window... sniffing, I expect.

thought: they look kitchen-capable
line: Ooh, you look like you know your way round a kitchen. Do you?

thought: calm people don't burn things, he imagines
line: You don't burn things, do you? You've a calm look about you.

thought: still going strong, unlike him
line: Still going strong, I see. Somebody ought to be.

thought: their life is what he'd do on a holiday he can't have
line: If I ever got a holiday, I'd spend it doing what you do.

thought: a helpful sort; he might ask after all
line: There goes a helpful sort. Not that I'd ask... well, I might.

thought: the goat dislikes everyone but would like this one
line: The goat would like you. The goat doesn't like anybody.

thought: they'd be a good kitchen hand
line: You'd make a fine kitchen hand, you know. Wasted on adventuring.

thought: an offer of food, not cake
line: If you're ever hungry, come by and I'll make you something. Not cake.

thought: adventurers go anywhere; he can't even get a holiday
line: You adventurers wander wherever you like. I can't even get a holiday.

thought: suspects them of being a salesman like the one who sold him the range
line: You're not a salesman, are you? Only the last one sold me that range.

thought: they've never offered to help in the kitchen
line: Look at that one. Never once offered to peel a potato.

thought: adventurers eat everything and never ask after the cook
line: You lot eat everything in sight and never ask how the cook is.

thought: even the goat helps more
line: The goat's more help in this kitchen than you've ever been.

thought: they look in for food; it's burnt and spoken for
line: Don't come in here after food. It's all burnt, and spoken for.

thought: adventurers knock things over
line: Mind your elbows near my pots. Adventurers are all elbows.

thought: the sea means eyepatches, which he dreads
line: Off to sea, are you? Rather you than me, with all those eyepatches.

thought: imagines himself sacked and thrown out
line: Thrown into the street, that's me. Hat and all.

thought: baffled a castle could run out of milk
line: A bucket of milk. How does a castle run out of a bucket of milk?

thought: he forgot the Duke's birthday ingredients
line: The Duke's birthday, and I forgot. Of all the days to forget.

thought: the mill is close but he can't leave
line: Millie's mill is just up the lane. It might as well be the moon.

thought: hopes the Duke won't notice no egg; knows he will
line: Maybe the Duke won't notice a cake without an egg. He will, won't he?

thought: nobody but the goat to mind the kitchen
line: I can't even go for flour. Who'd mind the kitchen, the goat?

thought: watches passers-by for an egg
line: Everyone walking past, and not one of them carrying an egg.

thought: hopes stillness will avert questions
line: If I stand very still, maybe nobody will ask about the cake.

thought: they look like they'd know where a cow is
line: You look the capable sort! The sort who'd know where a cow is.

thought: this one wouldn't let him be sacked
line: You'd not let a man be thrown into the street. I can tell.

thought: points them out as an egg-finder
line: That one looks like they could find an egg blindfolded.

thought: dragon-finders can surely find an egg
line: Adventurers find dragons, don't they? An egg must be nothing to you.

thought: the Duke would trust them with his cake
line: You've the look of someone the Duke would trust with his cake.

thought: steady hands, never dropped an egg
line: Ooh, steady hands. I bet you've never dropped an egg in your life.

thought: someone like this could save a birthday
line: If anyone could save a birthday, it'd be someone like you.

thought: he's sure they have a bucket on them somewhere
line: Somewhere about you there's a bucket. I can feel it.

thought: they walk past his crisis
line: Walking past a man in crisis. That's adventurers for you.

thought: sulky: don't mind him losing his job
line: Oh, don't mind me. I'm only about to lose my job.

thought: goblin-killing over the Duke's cake
line: Off killing goblins while the Duke's cake goes unmade, I suppose.

thought: they'd step over an egg
line: You'd step right over an egg on the floor, wouldn't you?

thought: dragons fine, flour beyond them
line: Brave enough for dragons, but a pot of flour's beyond you, is it?

thought: certain they won't help; he'll be in the street
line: That one won't help, they never do. I'll be in the street by supper.

thought: the one day he needs an adventurer, he gets this one
line: The one day I need an adventurer, and I get you.

thought: they sniff the air; nothing is cooking
line: Don't stand there sniffing. Nothing's cooking, nothing at all.

thought: still savours being saved
line: Saved! I still say it to myself of a morning.

thought: the range and he are getting on, for once
line: The range is behaving, or I'm behaving. One of us is.

thought: keeps checking he hasn't been thrown out
line: Has anyone thrown me in the street? Not yet, and I keep checking.

thought: keeps spare flour now
line: Got a bit of flour put by now, just in case. One never knows.

thought: they may use his range; the goat may not
line: You can use my range whenever you like now. Not the goat, though.

thought: listing his suppliers, and this one among them
line: Eggs from the Groats, and the rest of it from you. I remember.

thought: job and hat kept; a good year
line: Kept my job, kept my hat. A good year in this kitchen.

thought: plans to buy ingredients ahead next time
line: Next time I'll buy the ingredients before the day.

thought: they saved his job and asked nothing for it
line: My friend! You saved my job, and never asked a thing for it.

thought: offers them his range
line: Help yourself to my range, my friend. You've earned it.

thought: points out his rescuer
line: That one saved me from the street. I'll not forget it.

thought: a cook in Lumbridge would do anything for them
line: Back again! There's a cook in Lumbridge who'd do anything for you.

thought: nobody fetches milk like them
line: Nobody brings a bucket of milk like you do, my friend.

thought: the kindest adventurer, among many hungry ones
line: The kindest adventurer I know, and I know a lot of hungry ones.

thought: told the goat about them; the goat was impressed
line: I told the goat about you. It stopped chewing for a whole minute.

thought: if they need a cook he's here, burning things
line: Need a cook, my friend? You know where I am, burning things.

thought: sulks that they saved him once and now walk past
line: You saved me once, and now you just walk past. I see how it is.

thought: they may use the range but burning is his job
line: Use the range by all means, only don't burn anything. That's my job.

thought: one egg shouldn't go to their head
line: You found an egg once. Don't let it go to your head, my friend.

thought: assumes they're back wanting cake
line: Look who's back, wanting a cake, I expect. They always want a cake.

thought: they arrive just as he'd tidied
line: Oh, it's you. I'd just got the kitchen tidy.

thought: fetched milk once and acts like they own the place
line: Fetched me milk once, and now you think you own the kitchen.

thought: the Duke prefers edible food to their cooking
line: I'd let you cook for the Duke, but he likes his food edible.

thought: they're back for another job; there are no more birthdays
line: Back for more? I've no more birthdays, I'm afraid.

thought: the old roof creaks with every one of its years
line: Two hundred and thirty years, this church. The roof feels them all.

thought: he avoids the bell ropes; Urhney still teases him about them
line: I keep clear of the bell ropes... Urhney never lets me forget.

thought: no letter from Draynor in a while
line: No letter from the Wise Old Man lately. I do hope he's keeping well.

thought: Urhney took the swamp; he got the church
line: Urhney took the swamp and left me the church. I got the better end.

thought: Saradomin made the world with his brothers, and is the tidy one
line: Saradomin made the world with his brothers. He's the tidy one.

thought: he always read the god wars as a parable
line: I always took the war of the gods for a parable, light against dark.

thought: Saradomin's following outgrows his pews
line: More followers than any other god, Saradomin. More than my pews hold.

thought: practising the wording of a blessing
line: Is it 'smile upon' or 'shine upon'? Smile, I think.

thought: a blessing for a traveller who seems good
line: Saradomin smile on you, traveller. You've a good light about you.

thought: relieved this one has surely heard of Saradomin
line: You've heard of Saradomin, I can tell. What a relief!

thought: the church is open to folk like this most of all
line: The church is always open, you know, and to good folk most of all.

thought: remarks to someone that here walks a decent soul
line: There walks a decent soul. One can usually tell.

thought: they'd be a good bearer of the Wise Old Man's letters
line: You'd make a fine letter-carrier for the Wise Old Man, I think.

thought: even the hermit Urhney might smile at them
line: Even Father Urhney might crack a smile for you, and he's a hermit.

thought: light against dark; they're on the side of light
line: Light against darkness, and you on the side of light, I'd guess.

thought: they passed his door without sneering
line: Bless you for passing my door without a sneer. Not everyone does.

thought: they look lost; surely they've heard of Saradomin
line: You have heard of Saradomin, I hope? Only you've that lost look.

thought: the church has been open for centuries; they might try it
line: This church has been open over two hundred years. You might try it.

thought: never seen this one in church
line: Never once set foot in church, that one. Saradomin forgive them.

thought: he'll pray for them, and means it pointedly
line: I'll pray for you... I think it's rather needed.

thought: hurrying past a house of Saradomin is noticed
line: Rushing past a house of Saradomin? He does notice, you know.

thought: they look like they'd get stuck up the bell ropes, as he did
line: You look like you'd get stuck up a bell rope. Takes one to know one.

thought: Zamorakians rush like that; surely not this one
line: Zamorakians rush about like that. Not that you're one, I'm sure.

thought: a short sermon would help
line: A short sermon would do you good, traveller, a very short one.

thought: prayers and holy water failed; now he's ignoring it
line: I've tried prayers and holy water. Now I'm trying ignoring it.

thought: Urhney is the ghost expert, but won't leave the swamp
line: Urhney's the expert on ghosts. If only he'd come out of that swamp.
